name: Hezro
overview: Hezro was a male warrior known as the Carmelite and is listed as the twenty-ninth of "the thirty" mighty men who served King David. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, he is recognized for his distinguished role among David's elite fighters as recorded in 2 Samuel 23:35. There are no additional notes regarding his life or deeds beyond this designation.
namesAndTitles: The name Hezro appears as a proper name in Scripture without any given meaning or special title. It is simply recorded in 2 Samuel 23:35 as the name of one of David's notable warriors.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Hezro beyond his identification as one of David's thirty mighty men. No further relational details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hezro's significance lies in his inclusion among David's elite group of warriors, known as "the thirty," who were instrumental in supporting David's reign and military successes. His designation as "the Carmelite" may indicate a geographical or clan association, highlighting the diversity and strength of David's forces. Though little else is known, his mention affirms the faithfulness and valor of those who served God's anointed king.
